relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container registers a named callback contract under components.callbacks so that operations can attach the same outbound webhook interaction by reference instead of redefining it inline.
relationships.evidence: The OpenAPI document has an entry under components.callbacks/<name>, and at least one operation's callbacks map uses $ref: '#/components/callbacks/<name>' to point at it.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container holds a named sample value under components.examples, which media types, parameters or headers can pull into their examples maps by reference.
relationships.evidence: The document declares components.examples/<name> with a value or externalValue, and an examples map elsewhere contains $ref: '#/components/examples/<name>'.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container registers a named link descriptor under components.links so that several responses can share the same mapping from response values onto a follow-on operation's parameters.
relationships.evidence: The document defines components.links/<name> with an operationId or operationRef, and one or more response links maps reference it via $ref: '#/components/links/<name>'.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container holds a named request payload definition under components.requestBodies that multiple body-bearing operations can adopt as their requestBody by reference.
relationships.evidence: The document lists components.requestBodies/<name> with a content map, and operations declare requestBody: { $ref: '#/components/requestBodies/<name>' }.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container registers a named HTTP outcome under components.responses that operations can reuse for a status code, such as a shared 404 or error response.
relationships.evidence: The document defines components.responses/<name> with a description and optional content, and an operation's responses map assigns a status code to $ref: '#/components/responses/<name>'.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container owns a named header declaration in its components.headers registry, and that declaration exists only as an entry of the registry, ready to be referenced from response or encoding headers maps.
relationships.evidence: The document contains components.headers/<Header-Name> with a schema, and a response or encoding headers map points at it with $ref: '#/components/headers/<Header-Name>'.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container owns a named path, query, header or cookie parameter definition in components.parameters, which operations and path items include by reference.
relationships.evidence: The document declares components.parameters/<name> with name, in and schema, and a parameters array in an operation or path item includes $ref: '#/components/parameters/<name>'.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container is claimed to contain the document's path map, even though the endpoint set is defined at the document root and not within the components registry.
relationships.evidence: The parsed OpenAPI document would have to place the paths object inside components, whereas a valid document declares paths as a root-level sibling of components.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container owns each named Response definition in components.responses as an entry of that registry, and the entry serves as the canonical single-status-code outcome that operations reference.
relationships.evidence: The document's components.responses map has a keyed Response object, which an operation's responses map reaches through a '#/components/responses/<name>' $ref.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container is claimed to contain a status-code-keyed outcome map, although Responses objects are scoped to individual operations and components only registers individual Response entries.
relationships.evidence: The document would need a status-code-keyed Responses map placed inside components, whereas a valid document places that map under each operation's responses field.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container owns each named data-shape definition in components.schemas, and these entries act as the shared models that request bodies, responses, parameters and other schemas reference.
relationships.evidence: The document defines components.schemas/<Name> as a Schema Object, and media types, parameters or other schemas reference it via $ref: '#/components/schemas/<Name>'.

relationships.description: The reusable-definitions container owns each named credential mechanism in components.securitySchemes, such as an API key, HTTP bearer, OAuth2 or OpenID Connect scheme, and root-level or operation-level security requirements invoke the scheme by its name.
relationships.evidence: The document declares components.securitySchemes/<name> with a type, and a root or operation security array lists that <name> as a key.

notes: Response appears under both aggregates and composes, so the two edges are redundant and contradictory. The composes.paths edge is wrong: Paths is a root sibling of components. The composes.responses edge is wrong: components holds Response entries, not operation-scoped Responses maps. Registry entries use aggregates for some kinds and composes for others, with no clear basis for the difference.
